title: From What to Why: A Multi-Agent System for Evidence-based Chemical Reaction Condition Reasoning
claim: A multi-agent system decomposes a hard prediction task into grounded, staged reasoning steps and outperforms all baselines across every metric.
layout: 2 panels: left workflow diagram flowing top to bottom, right radar chart
description: The left panel is a boxed workflow diagram. It starts at the top with reactant and product molecule structures, with a reaction arrow between them. A pixel-art General Chemist avatar sits beside the product. Arrows lead down to a Candidate Condition box with colored circle triples, and to a Main Functional Group box listing reactants, by-product and reaction type. A Multi-Agent Debate box holds four pixel-art agents and an inset of Multi-Step Reasoning with Knowledge, Evidence and Summary. A funnel labeled Selection takes votes and narrows to a Top-50 Condition box. A yellow Memory bar with Conversation and Reaction Report sits at the bottom. The right panel is a radar chart comparing ChemMAS with eight baselines on Top-1 and Top-5 accuracy for catalyst, solvents and reagents. The large blue ChemMAS polygon encloses all the others.
caption: Overview of ChemMAS. A collaborative multi-agent system for evidence-based reaction-condition reasoning from SMILES inputs. ChemMAS demonstrates strong versatility and delivers state-of-the-art performance on reaction condition reasoning.
abstract: The chemical reaction recommendation is to select proper reaction condition parameters for chemical reactions, which is pivotal to accelerating chemical science. With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), there is growing interest in leveraging their reasoning and planning capabilities for reaction condition recommendation. Despite their success, existing methods rarely explain the rationale behind the recommended reaction conditions, limiting their utility in high-stakes scientific workflows. In this work, we propose ChemMAS, a multi-agent system that reframes condition prediction as an evidence-based reasoning task. ChemMAS decomposes the task into mechanistic grounding, multi-channel recall, constraint-aware agentic debate, and rationale aggregation. Each decision is backed by interpretable justifications grounded in chemical knowledge and retrieved precedents. Experiments show that ChemMAS achieves 20-35% gains over domain-specific baselines and outperforms general-purpose LLMs by 10-15% in Top-1 accuracy, while offering falsifiable, human-trustable rationales, which establishes a new paradigm for explainable AI in scientific discovery.
